title: SEC.gov | Policy Statements
主要内容: The U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) regularly issues policy statements to clarify its positions on various regulatory matters. These statements provide guidance on topics such as the acceleration of registration statements for issuers with mandatory arbitration provisions, procedures for the use of certain authorities under the Securities Exchange Act of 1934, and custody of digital asset securities by special purpose broker-dealers. The SEC also addresses issues related to central counterparties, proxy voting responsibilities of investment advisers, and market structure innovation for thinly traded securities. These policy statements are often accompanied by federal register versions and may include requests for public comments. The information is organized by release number, date, and details, offering insights into the SEC's regulatory priorities and evolving approaches to securities law enforcement and market oversight. The SEC has issued a series of policy statements and regulatory guidance related to financial markets and structured finance activities. These statements include the Interagency Statement on Sound Practices Concerning Elevated Risk Complex Structured Finance Activities, which was released on May 9, 2006, and the extension of the comment period for the Interagency Statement on Sound Practices Concerning Complex Structured Finance Activities, which was filed on June 16, 2004. The SEC also issued a policy statement on subpoenas to members of the news media, effective April 12, 2006. These statements reflect the SEC's ongoing efforts to ensure transparency, compliance, and stability in financial markets. The documents are available for public comment, and the SEC has provided access to comments received for these proposals. The last reviewed or updated date for these policy statements is April 12, 2022.
